newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end up on late buying, cements.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end up on late buying, cements.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended higher on Wednesday on the back of a spurt of late buying, particularly in cement stocks, following a positive outlook for the sector, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index closed up 5.62 points, or 0.79 percent at 721.98 points. In the broader market, losers led gainers by 63 to 55, with 77 counters unchanged.

"In the last one hour of trading, there was steady buying in the cement sector and Telkom. It helped the index to strenghten after slightly easing on profit-taking at midsession," a broker with a local firm said.
"The strengthening Indonesian rupiah and a stable regional foreign exchange market today gave a boost to overall market sentiment," an analyst with a European securities firm said.
She added, however, that many investors were still sidelined although there was growing optimism that the region's currency woes were on the decline.

"If foreign exchange markets in the region continue to stabilise this week, I expect the (Jakarta) stock market will get a further boost," said Imam Budi Sarjito, an analyst with Bank Negara Securities.

Cement stocks such as Semen Gresik, Indocement and Semen Cibinong made strong gains in active late trading following improved sentiment on the sector and specific issues affecting each company, analysts said.
"Recent worries over possible cement oversupply appeared to be overdone," a cement analyst with a local brokerage said.
"News reports that the Forestry Minister has proposed to stop providing new licences to build new cement factories in Java may have also boosted sentiment on the sector," the analyst said.
Sentiment on Semen Cibinong got a boost following reports of a planned bonus issue, brokers said.
Selling interest was seen on few banking stocks such as Bank Danamon and Bank Niaga, brokers said.

Bank Danamon closed 25 rupiah lower after falling to a year low of 1,025 rupiah, with volume approaching 15 million shares on what brokers blamed on market speculation that the bank might report forex losses when it holds an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders in late August.

Danamon said earlier on Wednesday that it planned to hold an the meeting to seek approvals for proposed transactions with subsidiaries. A bank official later denied that it had suffered losses in currency trading.

Bank Niaga was down on news that Standard & Poor's may cut the bank's ratings, brokers said. It fell 50 rupiah to 7,700 rupiah with some one million shares traded after earlier touching an intra-day low of 7,550 rupiah.
Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it had placed the BB long-term and single-B short-term ratings of Bank Niaga on creditwatch with negative implications.
S&P said its move followed the announcement by Tirtamas Group of its plan to buy 50 percent of Bank Niaga.
"The possible ratings downgrade prompted the profit-taking," one broker said.

Bank Niaga made sharp gains earlier this week on news that privately-owned PT Tunasmas Paduarta, a unit of the Tirtamas Group, planned to acquire a 50 percent stake in the bank at 8,000 rupiah per share.
